findings: [P1] Duplicate comment IDs can promote unapproved text. packages/cadenda/beads_adapter.py accepts duplicate IDs; context_builder.py fetch() overwrites sources[ref] for each duplicate. Receipt verification uses next(), checking the first matching comment, but renders sources[ref], containing the last matching comment. A valid approved comment followed by an unapproved comment with the same ID therefore renders the latter as current approved requirements. Reject duplicate normalized comment IDs (including integer/string collisions), and render the exact comment whose hash was verified.

[P1] Failed graph reads bypass the traversal limit. packages/cadenda/context_builder.py limits its loop using len(issues), which increases only after successful issue retrieval. An issue containing many distinct nonexistent dependencies causes every dependency to be queried despite max_issues; each process can consume its own 20-second timeout. Count attempted issue reads against a shared traversal budget, including receipt-driven fetches, and report remaining references when exhausted.

[P2] Secret-bearing JSON keys bypass redaction and are persisted. packages/cadenda/security.py redact() sanitizes dictionary values but preserves keys unless a key exactly matches a credential field name. Beads models permit extra fields, and context_builder.py retains the complete raw payload. An extra field such as metadata={"sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123456":"value"} therefore persists that credential verbatim in snapshot sources and exposes it through paging. Sanitize arbitrary dictionary keys before persistence, handling resulting key collisions explicitly.
